comment.text:
My husband took me to Micklethwait for a late lunch on Saturday. I'd been to their trailer 5 or so years ago, but never to their permanent location. I also wasn't much of a meat eater back in those days, so I mostly had tried their sides. Now we're both on keto, so we go for just the meat. 

The meat was some of the best I've had lately! If I had one criticism, the brisket was just the slightest bit dry, but it had the perfect amount of fat to still make it taste good, and the smoky flavor was perfect! The turkey was moist, and probably my favorite part of the meal. We didn't order sides, but the included pickles were better than standard. 

It was rainy when we went there, so everyone was packed inside. There were barely enough tables. Their outside seating is not covered. There was no line, and my husband had finished our order by the time I had shaken out my umbrella.  The air conditioning was a little too cold for a rainy day. 

The parking lot is all designated handicapped parking, but we got street parking right next to the building. 

Since we live on the east side, Micklethwait is convenient, and it has earned a place among our favorite places to go eat!

The TLDR:   I would come back but ONLY for take out.  The potato salad is a rock star! 

We stopped by for a late lunch on a Saturday in August and may have just had some poor timing.  The weather was unbearably hot which also affected our visit because we couldn't eat outside. 

The issue:   The dining room is small and can only hold so many people.  We ordered quickly and the food was ready almost immediately.  But we had no where to sit!   So we stood there with food in hand (kinda in the way of the workers and other patrons) waiting for people to vacate.  Part of the problem was there were two tables occupied without any food and they were just talking.  At other places, this is awesome.  But a place with limited seating:  nope!  So our food was cold and the grits congealed while we waited to sit down. 

The service:  all of the staff we interacted with were kind, friendly, and helpful.  They were a highlight of our visit. 

The sides:   We had the Green Chili Grits and the Potato Salad.  Both were excellent but the potato salad was maybe the best I've ever had.  For me, it was perfection because it wasn't too "wet" and the dill was just a fantastic add. 
The meats:   We had the beef brisket and the sausage. Both were very good.  I preferred the sausage but maybe just got a less than perfect piece of the brisket. 

The parking:  also not great.  There is street parking but also a back lot they direct you to off of Springdale.  But they don't really have a safe/marked path to get you to the building.  Just loose gravel where you're at risk of an ankle sprain. 

Maybe they will consider expanding the inside space?   That would really help.   I'd still come back because the food was really fantastic, but only for take out where I wouldn't have to deal with parking or finding/waiting for a table.

Vibe: homey, cozy, Southern charm!
Service: line went pretty fast. you ordered at the front and can choose seating 

Items ordered: 
- 3 meat 2 sides plate, $30
Brisket 8.8/10, the cut we got was slightly dry today, but depending on the day, the brisket can be a 9.5/10
Pork ribs 8/10, a good, standard tender pork rib
Mac and cheese 9.5/10, SO GOOD! flavorful
Lemon poppy slaw 8/10, refreshing flavor
Banana pudding 6/10, the banana is blended within the pudding and nilla wafers aren't soaked in the pudding (my preference!)

I visited Micklethwait Barbecue in the mid-afternoon, which is usually a slower time for restaurants, and I was hoping to avoid the crowds. Luckily, there was no line, so I was able to order right away.

Both the indoor and outdoor seating areas are really nice. If I hadn't been on the road, I probably would have stayed and hung out a little longer, but I ended up getting takeout instead.

The Tex-Czech sausage was one of the most delicious sausages I've had at a BBQ restaurant. I absolutely loved the melted cheese inside the sausage. The brisket also hit the spot, and the sauce was amazing.

My only wish, or small complaint, is the portion size. It feels like shrinkflation may be part of it, and it's definitely not cheap. But for a once-in-a-while treat, Micklethwait is absolutely worth it.

I honestly debated whether to post about Micklethwait BBQ or keep this hidden gem to myself... but it's too good not to share! This spot was a standout on our Austin BBQ tour and completely lived up to the hype.

The brisket and sausage were both incredible, but the brisket especially stole the show. It was easily my favorite in Austin. The bark had the perfect texture and flavor, while the meat itself stayed unbelievably juicy and tender. Every bite was exactly what you hope for when you think of great Texas BBQ. The sausage was just as impressive, packed with flavor and cooked perfectly. You can tell there's real attention to detail here!

If you're putting together a BBQ tour in Austin, this place deserves a spot on your list. Part of me wants to gatekeep it, but it's just too good not to recommend!!

Watch this spot grow from its food truck days to a large brick n mortar. It remains one of Austin's shining stars.

If you're doing a BBQ tour or introducing central Texas bbq to guests, this place should be in rotation.

P.S. The pecan mesquite cookie is something. Get one.

comment.text:
Perhaps the most gentile installment in the Austin BBQ milieu - it is, after all, housed in a converted church. Way out on the edges of deep east Austin, sort of where civilization gives way to wilderness (in fact, I espied a group of guys in a nearby wooded thicket - not homeless, but certainly poor - hanging out around a campfire as though the 19th century never ended). In this Tom Sawyer Island universe there is a white clapboard chapel, rows of smokers, and piles of oak. 

At Micklethwait, the bill o' fare matches the scenery. Food tastes wholesome. Contrast a place like la BBQ, which has an edge of provocation, the food their containing perhaps more spices than you would like.

Micklethwait tastes like what you'd imagine the early German and Czech practitioners were after. You taste smoke and beef and everything else is superfluous. The brisket strikes a balance between toothsomeness and suavity. 

They have other meats beyond the Central Texas canon of brisket, ribs and sausage. Unfortunately, I couldn't manage to eat any more than the staples. A very pleasant side dish is the green bean salad. Charred green beans are then chilled and ultimately tossed in what seemed was crispy quinoa and a lemon vinaigrette. With all the smoke, beef, booze and cheese laden Tex-Mex in Austin, these green beans stuck out like legumes from some celestial patch.

I have had Micklethwait bookmarked since it was a food truck so it has to be a couple of years. Well, today was the day that I could unbook mark Micklethwait and a gorgeous day to take advantage of their plentiful outside seating/dining area.
 
I arrived at approximately 1300 and there was not a line hopefully meaning that the meat was still on the menu and not sold out. 

I ordered the Tex-Czech sausage, Pork Spareribs, and Moist Beef Brisket with Mac and Cheese and Braised Greens with Bacon for my sides.

Tex-Czech sausage is house-made and is quite flavorful with a snap that I love.

The Pork Sparerib was perfectly smoked with a nice rub and I love it when I can chew the grisle without loosening teeth.

The Moist Beef Brisket was perfect with a nice smoke ring and the bark was perfect and flavorful.

All in all, I thoroughly enjoyed my lite afternoon snack and I will definitely be back to check out the lamb and some of their other house-made sides like the Lemon-Poppy Slaw and Citrus Beet Salad.

comment.text: Wow.  Brisket melted, just melted in your mouth.  I don't think I needed to chew.  Very moist and tasty.  Ribs were good as were the sides and sausage.  They designed an old church with mostly outdoor seating but decent amount of indoor seating.  The place isn't large by Texas standards.  We went off peak around 2pm ish and didn't wait long to order.  Staff were helpful and friendly.

For my first bbq place to go in Texas, I chose it to be Micklethwait so I had high expectations!   I came about a hour before closing so a few items including some of the sides ran out.   I got the 3 meats and 2 sides platter.  I had their brisket, pulled pork, and cheesy link sausage.   For the sides I had Cole slaw and potato salad.   I definitely enjoyed everything I had, my favorite was the sausage!

I enjoyed my time at Micklethwait Barbecue.  The place wasn't that busy when I went which is definitely nice.  Most barbecue spots in Austin have crazy long lines and run out of food when you arrive.  So I enjoyed going to a spot that was more laid back.  The service was fantastic.  They have nice seating options both indoors and outdoors.  The outdoor seating gives you that authentic Austin feel as if you are sitting in a coffee shop.  The food was solid.  I tried the 3 meat and 2 sides plate with brisket, pulled lamb, sausage, beans and Mac & cheese.  The sausage by far was my favorite.  The pulled lamb was different, which I enjoyed.  You just don't see this as an option offered on most menus.  Overall, it was a great experience!

comment.text:
We came to Micklethwait from multiple friends' recommendations during our week-long trip San Antonio to Austin. It was fantastic!

For 2 people, we ordered the brisket, pork ribs, cheesy hot link, with mac n cheese and green beans sides. I normally don't prefer dry rub ribs, but they were amazing, so flavorful. The green beans were also perfect and a great tangy compliment to the meats. We were really impressed by the cheesy hot link - it was staff-recommended since they're known for their sausages.

We came in around noon on a Friday, and we waited a bit to order but not long - and the food is prepared immediately. Staff were so friendly, helpful and welcoming - we would definitely return for the service (and the food).

The indoor and outdoor seating areas are both really nice - great space for groups. Parking was also not hard to find on their street.

The flavors of Micklethwait were really unforgettable, and we hope to return soon!

As always, Micklethwait continues to be a solid choice for bbq in Austin, especially if you want indoor seating and a quickly moving line. Plenty of parking in the lot and nearby neighborhood roads. You get in, wait in line if needed, order at the counter, and then wait for your food. My fiancé and I live close by and have gone over a few times to grab a lunch special on Thursdays or Fridays ($15 for a bbq meat sandwich, a side, and a sweet tea). The food is so tasty and fresh, and always consistently good! 

The only confusing part is sometimes they've given the side in essentially a Dixie cup (super super small) and other times in a plastic container (still small, but enough for one person). 

Either way, this place is solid and dependable and I will definitely be back!

comment.text: This place is underrated in a city with many barbeque options. The prices were of great value and didn't disappoint. The brisket was moist, Smokey, well seasoned and traditional to most briskets in the area. The sausage had a good snap to it, peppery and Smokey. The ribs had a good bite to it, and wasn't fall off the bone but the bone came out clean. I must say though, the jalapeño cheese grits was a nice change up for sided offerings. The smoked duck and sausage gumbo was also delicious and still tasted great when I took it home to reheat as I had ordered too much food. Their smoked lamb shoulder was moist and was absolutely a must have if available as it was the special that day. The location is nice, parking is a little limited but they had great indoor and outdoor seating options. The service was excellent and they operated quickly for taking and delivering orders.

comment.text:
We showed up at 11am on a Friday, fully expecting to have to struggle to find parking and to have to wait in a line for who knows how long. But that wasn't the case at all! We just parked in the front and were able to immediately make our way to the front counter. In fact, the workers there had to wait on us while we chose which menu items we wanted. 

For those reasons above, Micklethwait is already worth the visit because you save so much time. But the food is really good too! I will say, it's not the best bbq I've ever had in my life with items that make your jaw drop. But it's a really solid place to go when you're craving some reliable bbq! 

And I really love the plate options. I came with one friend, and although there weren't many of us, we wanted to try a bunch of different meats and sides without going overboard. So we were able to get two 2 meat plates, meaning we were able to try 4 meats and 4 sides without breaking the bank. And we still had lots to take home with us too. 

The jalapeño cheddar sausage actually might be my favorite meat that we tried! Followed by the ribs, and then the brisket and pulled lamb. I do wish the brisket and pulled lamb were a little juicier, but both were still really good. 

And the mac n cheese, beet salad, and cheesy grits are all sides I would get again. The bread it comes with is also homemade and is so so yummy. 

Plus the workers were so friendly. Even when we were leaving, they remembered us by name when they said goodbye.

I've been enjoying Micklethwait Craft Meats for years, and this past fall when my wife and I were planning our wedding reception, we contacted Micklethwait about catering.

The whole process was so easy and they did an amazing job bringing in all of the food for our guests. It was great to have a selection of brisket, sausage, and turkey, as well as delicious sides: Campfire Chili Beans, Herbed Potato Salad, Mac and Cheese, and Farmers Market Green Salad.

Plus, they brought in fantastic banana pudding for dessert. I would 100% book them for an event, again, and I look forward to my next lunch at Micklethwait!

Micklethwait absolutely shocked me not just for the quality of meat, but the thoughtful modern/rustic setting, staff, and the fact that I only had to wait behind a small handful of people on the 4th of July to get some awesome BBQ. 

I have eaten at... 10? Of the top BBQ places in and around Austin. And if you said "Hey you are going back and you can only eat at 1 or 2 this trip" then Micklethwait is at the very top of the list of places to hit. The sides (especially the grits) rock. All the meat is as you would expect, world class.

Literally the best bbq place anywhere in the country. Best friendly service! Best meat cuts! Best meat choices! They got lamb and pastrami too?! Cute location. There is an outdoor location too. Their staff were so attentive and even one of them overheard that we ran out of pickles without us asking and came over with a bowl of sliced pickles. What a joy! And their pickles tasted freshly made. Avoid the crowds in other places and go here!

Had the BRISKET and PORK RIBS --chef's kiss! All the sides are a must-try, and the staff couldn't be friendlier. ENJOY! 

PS: Parking lot is quite small, street pakring is going to be best.

Finally got around to checking Micklethwait out. It's a little off the beaten path, which meant there were only 4-5 people ahead of me in line when I pulled up on Sunday morning, when they opened at 11 am. 

Was a little disappointed to learn that they no longer sell tacos  but the Frito Pie made up for it.

TLDR: Charming East Austin spot with friendly service. Solid food across the board for a fair price; great house bread/pickles are a nice touch. Very good, but not quite a destination.

Overview:
Micklethwait Barbecue (the "th" is silent) brings classic Central Texas barbecue vibes to a charming little chapel-like spot in East Austin. From the gravel garden patio with lush plants to the minimalist interior with wood floors and sleek ceiling fans, the setting is relaxed and welcoming. There's a small parking lot plus plenty of street parking, and the service, which was warm, attentive, and never overbearing, is genuinely A+. They offer some additional practical perks as well: big self-serve water jugs and bug spray for patio diners.

Food:
I went for the three-meat plate (brisket, spare ribs, and a Tex-Czech sausage) with lemon-poppy coleslaw and mac & cheese, plus banana pudding for dessert. Prices are fair for Austin right now: brisket $34/lb, ribs $30/lb, sausage $27/lb, sides $6/8 oz, and the three-meat plate at $28. The brisket is the headliner: peppery bark, juicy slices with nicely rendered fat, and clean beef flavor. The spare ribs were flavorful and very juicy, just a bit tougher than ideal. The Tex-Czech sausage had a satisfying snap and good seasoning, though the interior was a bit dense/tough. Both sides were great: the lemon-poppy slaw was bright and refreshing (great palate reset between bites of smoke), and the mac & cheese tasted like a well-executed homemade version that is comforting and not bland. Also, don't skip the in-house bread; it's genuinely good enough to eat on its own, and their pickles are crisp and tangy, the kind of small detail that elevates a tray. The banana pudding is a simple, from-scratch take with Nilla wafers and whipped cream; I'd prefer it to be a bit more banana-forward, but it was still a pleasant finish.

Final Thoughts:
This is a very strong, very Austin barbecue experience: excellent brisket, well-made sides, thoughtful little touches, and warm service in a beautiful, low-key setting. While not every bite hit "destination" level for me, the overall quality and value make it an easy recommendation, especially if you want classic Central Texas barbecue executed with care.

comment.text:
I recently visited Austin and stopped by Micklethwait for some bbq. It did not disappoint! There was a little bit of a line, but the line was only inside (I was told it routinely flows outside on busy days). The line moved quickly, so we got to the front in no time. While we were waiting, I enjoyed peeking at everyone's tables to see what they had ordered. Everything looked and smelled incredible!

By the time we got to the front of the line, they had run out of pulled lamb and Mac n cheese. We were surprised because we arrived about an hour and a half after opening! We ordered brisket, pork ribs, sausage, and sides of beans, grits, and slaw. We really wanted Mac n cheese but because it was sold out, we couldn't get it.

The food was incredible. The brisket melted in my mouth, the rib meat fell off the bone, and the sausage was smoky and perfectly seasoned. The sides were also delicious: the beans had a hint of spice, the slaw was refreshing, and the grits were amazing. The free pickles were also really good. While we were eating, an employee mistakenly brought an order of Mac n cheese to our table (they had cooked another batch). We reluctantly told her that she had the wrong table, and a few minutes later, she came back and gave us a free side of Mac n cheese. It was amazing!!

The inside of the restaurant is clean and comfortable with beautiful plants. There is also outdoor seating and plenty of street parking.

I HIGHLY recommend this place if you're in the mood for some bbq in Austin!

comment.text:
For a Sunday in Austin, TX, some people head to church where I decided to head over to the Meat Church.  From its early food trailer beginnings, Micklethwait Barbecue has now upgraded and moved into a former old church building in east Austin.  They operate Thu - Sun, and are located on the busy Springdale Rd @ Tanney St, east of Airport Blvd.  Parking is available on the neighborhood streets. The owner Tom Micklethwait is a Texas native and Austin local started his food truck in East Austin back in 2012.  They have made the highly coveted Texas Monthly Top 50 BBQ list in 2017 & 2021 (and I bet will make it again for 2025).  Micklethwait is serving up traditional Texas bbq, with some unique specials, a variety of sides and awesome desserts.  The new building in east Austin offers indoor or outdoor seating, plenty of shade, and great service.

I ordered a two meat plate which comes with two sides.  My order came with brisket, pork spare ribs, mac & cheese, and jalapeno grits.  They also serve two different styles of sausage, turkey, occasional beef ribs, and smoked pulled lamb.  The choice of sides come from chili beans, potato salad, beet salad and several others.  Mickelthwait will also serve items like Frito Pie, Elotes, and smoked half chicken.  The desserts choices give the options of banana pudding, pecan cookie or freshly made moon pies.  The brisket is oak smoked, very tender with solid bark and seasoning.  Pork spare ribs are tender, well cooked, and also properly seasoned.  The mac & cheese sides are of a good cheese melt, and the jalapeno grits are a southern specialty.  They serve fresh bread, offer two different styles of bbq sauce, and are serving different specials year round.
 
Micklethwait has been open since 2012 and continues to be one of the top spots for Austin TX bbq.  I have said before that in Austin, we have such a wide variety of choices to get top level BBQ, that it can be hard to choose which place you want to venture to.  Micklethwait might not be as large as the other spots, but they are serving proper Texas style bbq with amazingly friendly service. It is Texas BBQ style to the core!  You can tell their crew works more as a family and operates a very well run establishment.  The food is fantastic, but add in the friendly service they offer, this place is a true staple for Texas bbq!

I've been wanting to come here for a couple years now and after hearing that the owners opened a brick and mortar store earlier this year, I thought now would be a great time. Upon arrival, the line was not very long at 10:40 in the morning (less than 10 people) and it went by pretty quick. For the main course my family and I got the Brisket, Turkey Breast, Pulled Lamb, Green Chile Chorizo, and Beef Ribs. For the sides, we got the Herbed Potato Salad, Lemon Poppy Slaw, Squash Salad, and the Green Chile Grits. And finally for dessert we got a Pecan Mesquite Bean Cookie. 

The Turkey Breast was great, the seasoning had a strong peppercorn flavor and the meat was both smoky and juicy. The Beef Ribs had a nice bark and tasted like a cross between a top sirloin steak and a brisket, it was also very tender, and was a little moist. The Green Chile Chorizo Sausage some hints of garlic in the blend and the chiles really came through with regard to taste, the casing was also snappy, and the sausage was also moist. Unfortunately, the same could not be said with the Brisket and the Pulled Lamb. The Brisket was tender and seasoned but was pretty dry and the Pulled Lamb was pretty stringy and lacked juiciness as well. That is not to say they were not smoky from the oak they use, but the texture really brings down both dishes. 

With regard to the sides, the Lemon Poppy Slaw was very finely chopped and had wonderful floral and sweet notes with an addition of what tasted a little like mint which paired wonderfully with the meat. The Squash Salad had both yellow and calabaza squash with some corn, it was nice and crispy and a little sweet as well, the texture really reminded me of a fresh cucumber salad. The Green Chile Grits were phenomenal, and had a strong cheddar flavor with pops of spice from the green chiles which really balanced the richness from the dish. The Herbed Potato Salad was not really the best, while it had onions, celery, and parsley, it could have been salted more and it lacked some acidity. Both the pickles along with the pickled red onions were very standard, they were fresh, crispy, and tangy. Ending off on a positive note was the Pecan Mesquite Bean Cookie, it had a nice and rich toffee-like flavor and had hints of cinnamon and coffee notes. On top of that it was gooey with a crisp exterior with pecans and chocolate chips to add an extra sweet and crunchy element to the dessert. 

All in all, the food had some really great hits but also some hard misses. That being said, the restaurant is very clean and has a comforting and relaxing ambiance. Moreover, the service was quick and the staff was very friendly. Personally, I'll come back as they are probably trying to get used to operating in a new location. But as of right now, I would say they need to work on having juicer BBQ.

30 min wait at 1:30pm on Thursday

They just ran out of the ribs prior to our arrival which I wanted to try :( it's a cute place. 

Pulled brisket sandwich: meats dry but the flavor's good.

Beets: really yummy and goes fantastic with the meat.

The combination of the beets with the bbq took this from a 4 to a 6/10 for me.

Invited to a soft opening at the new location on Tanney St., in Austin. As you can imagine there was a line, yet everyone waiting was in good spirits.  It didn't take too long to get inside. 

Tom Micklethwait truly has smoking meat down to a craft. They offer brisket, sausage, turkey, pork, beef and lamb. 

When i judge a BBQ restaurant, the quality of the sides has to match the effort put into the meat. The evidence is there. Macaroni and cheese, greens, beans, fresh green beans, chile cheese grits and the freshest bread I've ever experienced with BBQ. Then there are the desserts, banana pudding, a home made fudge brownie and others. 

Micklethwait has taken his craft to the next level. Price, taste, value and ambiance. All the boxes are checked. 
One thing I noticed was that the staff was working in harmony. No one seemed stressed out or over whelmed. Polite, friendly and sincere. 

There is seating inside, with a huge outdoor seating area outside. 

So head on over to East Austin and give them a try. Parking may be a bit of a challenge. Street parking is available, so be respectful of the neighbors. 

Michael C. - Georgetown, Tx.

Came in for an early lunch on a Sunday. We were first in line (we overestimated the line situation for sure); did not need to arrive an hour early lol. Went with a beef rib (Sunday only) and a 2 meat platter with turkey, lamb, beans, and cheddar jalapeno grits. The platter had 2 slices of turkey; one was dry the other was juicy and delicious. The lamb was rich and flavorful, and the beef rib was an indulgent treat. However, the sides fell flat for us. Jalapeno cheddar grits lacked flavor other than cream, and the beans were also thick and not very flavorful. The staff was super friend, the interior is clean with nice bathrooms, and they have a huge, nice patio. If I could go for 4.5 stars I would. Giving 5 because my husband loved it and the owner was super nice when we spoke with her during our wait. Come for the meat, maybe opt for different sides or make your own.

comment.text: Got here at 11AM on a Sunday when the doors opened and the wait wasn't too bad at all. (15 mins?) The place is super cute, the service is friendly, the price is fair, and the food is amazing. The sides were unique without being "over the top unique." Everything was solid and we had a great time. 5 stars!

My favorite Austin BBQ spot.  The brisket is consistently incredibly flavorful and perfectly crusted.  They always have unique meat offerings (venison, lamb, etc.) and amazing sides.

The texture of their beets is perfect, their bbq sauces are homemade and so damn fine.

There is almost always a line, but it moves very fast!  The service is great, and the outdoor seating is ample.

comment.text: Food was really good overall. Few items were out when we first got in line, but they were restocked by the time we ordered. Loved the pork ribs, and the sides were solid. The cheeseburger was the standout, smoked half-pound patty with just pickles and sauce, and honestly better than most burger spots in Austin. Definitely coming back.

Amazing! It was unanimous. The three of us agreed it was the best BBQ we ever had. The biggest hits were the brisket and sausage. The cabbage, turkey, and pork ribs were delicious too. 

Friendly and patient service. Not too busy. Indoor and outdoor seating.

The potato salad and brisket was the best for this place. I would say overall, the food is 4.7, the sausages were somehow very dry this time.

Service was excellent, we ordered online and it was timely.

The place was in a shaded tent area. The benches were clean and long enough to fit a crowd.

The restaurant settings is one of the lovelier spaces for BBQ that I have seen in Austin. It is spread out, and the outdoor area is under trees and perfect to enjoy the feast you have likely ordered. Wait times also are not terrible. We arrived around 11:30 a.m. on a Sunday and did not wait more than 15 minutes. We ordered the wet brisket, pulled lamb, pork ribs, and turkey. The turkey was surprisingly tasty - and I would recommend not skipping. The pulled lamb was also surprisingly tender and flavorful. Overall, everything was good - but it was not the best BBQ in Austin that I have had. Sides were quite tasty, including the mac and cheese, slaw and beets. The pecan cookies is NOT to be missed!
Came here with a few buddies from work. Do not pas on the lamb... customer service was great. Employees were very hospitable and friendly. BBQ is good but they had a menu of sides that are amazing

Such a good barbecue spot! Definitely aim to go there off peak hours so you don't have to wait as long. The patio is great. I wish there was more parking but you can drink around and look for street parking. The poppyseed slaw and mac and cheese were good. The potato salad was lacking favor. The brisket is super tasty but the pork ribs were a teeny bit dry. I'd definitely come back.

If ever a restaurant needed a soup nazi, this place is it. I'll get to the food details momentarily. Let's chat first about a behind the counter operation dying for a six sigma expert to come in and remove the sludge. The lack of hustle on the part of the counter staff was exceeded only by the lack of decisiveness by the customers. An angry tyrant with a bushy mustache, cracking the whip, would've benefited all parties equally.

Our party of three saw no one moving quickly, despite a long line. Maybe they were all stoned? I have nothing against that, by the way. To be fair, many BBQ joints in Austin suffer from the same service problem. This has always puzzled me because everything in a BBQ joint is premade. All they need to do is slice, scoop, and serve. So why does it take 45 minutes to get to the counter and place your order? (For reference, we started in line outside with 8 people ahead of us and roughly 30ish people inside).

If you have been to Style Switch or Terry Black's, you've seen efficiency in action. Maybe these folks need to take a visit there and get a mentor.

Onto the main event! We ordered pulled lamb, a beef rib, and pork spare ribs. We also got the side dish platter. We selected green chili grits, mac and cheese, and a lemon poppy slaw. As a side note, we also got frozen lemonades and a pilsner from Meanwhile Brewing - nice local touch there.

The lamb is what they're known for, so I'll tell you it's good. Is it worth going back for? Not really. The beef rib was so well seasoned and had a nice bark. Most excellent. The pork ribs were also tasty. As for the sides and drinks, I can say the sides were pretty, pretty pretty good (thanks, Larry David). I mean, I don't even like grits, but we ordered them because so many Yelpers raved about them. Let me tell ya, they ain't lying. The lemonade was incredible. And no, not like in the standard Yelp description you get from so many. It was the perfect balance of sour and sweet. The sour leads the palate and that is how it should be.

Overall, food was tasty and on par with most Austin BBQ. Service was friendly, but annoyingly slow. The inside of the restaurant is clean and has a good vibe. The outdoor area is where we ate and there was space aplenty.

Should you check this place out? Yes. Will we return anytime soon? No.

Nut allergy friendly! Nothing I ordered had any issues and I don't think they have anything with nuts.

First off, Google Maps takes you to a weird spot. They do have some parking.

We got in around 11:30AM on a Sunday and were shocked that there was no line after driving by the absurdity that is Franklin's. I came with an 18-pack of beer prepared to share with people! Anyway... They do have a bar at Saddle Up.

It took 22 minutes for us to receive the buzzer notification for our Family Pack (5-6 people). We added a 0.5lb of the lamb. I'd definitely do the beef rib here if I return. 

Anyway, that family pack fed 9 people comfortably! Everyone had their own favorites. Online it says that they give 3 quarts of sides but on site I was offered 4 pints so I'm not sure which is correct. 

Highlights were the cucumber salad and grits for the sides, and the sausage for meats. Their spicy barbecue sauce was also phenomenal.

Will happily return to try their beef rib some day.

My meal was pure fat.  The brisket was inedible because it was so fatty.  The sausages also way too fatty.  I can't believe they would have even served me that brisket because it was obviously nothing a person should eat.  I ate what sides I could, went home, and had something else to eat.

I cannot believe we live across the street from this glorious meat oasis.
The macaroni and cheese is everything you expect it to be in the South.
The brisket tacos pack so much taste it's like a burst of absolute bliss to mouths
The sausage sandwich is the stuff dreams are made of.
Great service.
Fun, outdoor, family-style seating.
Located behind Saddle Up.

Solid barbecue served by the nicest people in airy and inviting surroundings. The brisket was a bit too fatty for me but the ribs were tender and tasty and even better was the moist and delicious turkey. My daughter also gave rave reviews for the lamb and liked the poblano sausage. Absolutely loved the potato salad and green bean sides, but the best part of the meal was the banana pudding finish, it was the best I've ever had!

Micklethwait is a bbq place that serves its food via a food truck. They have outdoor seating with fans and free water. 

I came on a Thursday during lunch time. The wait was not that long at all, and I got my food fairly quickly. 

I decided to get the 2 meat plate, but I also liked that they had options for other mains like tacos. For the 2 meat plate, I got brisket and pulled lamb with a side of beans and jalapeño cheese grits. 

The brisket was so tender and juicy. The lamb was also delicious and easy to eat. They both paired well with the sauces on the table. Grits aren't exactly my favorite but the jalapeño grits definitely are one of the better grits I've had. It is not spicy at all though, more cheesy if anything. The beans were good. Felt satisfied by the end of the meal.

photos.caption: Brisket and Lamb, Jalapeo Cheese Grits, Beans

comment.text:
Thursday 7/25/2024

I was highly interested in this spot due to it being the highest rated bbq spot on google and yelp. Also word of my mouth from the people in Austin grew my anticipation even more. On my first visit to Austin in 2023, I missed out on going but this time I finally went. 

The service was pretty great as she was nice and very helpful. 
Also the pricing was pretty good to as it's one of the only Texas bbq spots (I've been to) that let you order the meat through 2 meat plates or 3 meat plates rather than straight up by the pound.

For my visit, I got a 2 meat plate of brisket & ribs with sides of mac n cheese & beans $20, 1/4 pork shoulder $6.50, and 1/4 pulled lamb $7.

- The Mac n cheese was pretty underwhelming, it was okay but it didn't have a lot of flavor for me.
- The beans were alright but they weren't the beans I was expecting from a Texas bbq spot, I was more so expecting a bbq beans type of side.
- The ribs and brisket were very tender and they were a solid choice but I've had better.
- The pork shoulder really impressed me as I did not expect it to be that good. I'd honestly say it was the star of the show as the flavor and taste were on point.
- The pulled lamb also impressed me as it was way better than I expected and I would say it was the second best item I had.
- the sauces were underwhelming as well, they were just okay but not good in my opinion. 

All in all, micklethwait is a pretty decent bbq spot but I can't say it's the best Texas bbq I've had. If you were to visit, I would highly recommend you at least get the pork shoulder and pulled lamb as those were quite the surprise for me.

photos.caption: 2 meat plate of brisket and pork ribs with Mac & cheese and beans $20 AND 1/4 pork shoulder $6.50 AND 1/4 pulled lamb $7

comment.text:
I don't think it's my favorite BBQ spot but there are some notable items here (mostly the sides).

Brisket - Solid brisket, I did find my pieces to have too thick of a fat slice between them. I usually like a more moist fatty brisket, but the fat was a bit much I think. And I would've liked if the rest of the brisket was more moist.

Beef Ribs - these were good, they didn't fall of the bone with moisture as much as I'd like but they did come off pretty easily.

Sausage - I actually really enjoyed the sausage, very juicy and tasty!

Lemon Poppy Slaw - probably the best slaw I've ever had at a BBQ spot. I usually get tired of slaw when it's either too creamy or too vinegary, but these really hit the spot and worked perfectly with the meats when put in sandwiches.

Herbed Potato Salad - might also be the best potato salad I've had as well! It was almost mashed liked mashed potatoes but with still some chunks of potato (but softened). It was also really refreshing and I didn't tire of it at all as I continued eating it.

Their sides here really shone, even though I think the BBQ wasn't the best I've had in Austin and didn't really excel in any particular meat.

photos.caption: Herbed Potato Salad and Lemon Poppy Slaw - some of my fave sides of any BBQ spot

comment.text: Food was amazing, truly dangerously good! And beautiful new location- inside and out. Outside is shaded, tables and chairs, fans, flowers, lights. A lovely experience all around.

By far, Micklethwait was our favorite meal of our Houston and Austin trip. We got the 3 meat + 2 sides plate. We selected pork ribs, brisket, sausage, grits, and cabbage. The brisket and grits were the stars of the plate, but everything else was tasty too. 

We arrived around 11:50 AM on Thursday, and there was only 1 person ahead of us in line. By the time we had finished around 12:20, there was about ten people in line. If the line had been shorter, we would've gone back for seconds. 

All in all, we were very impressed with the food, especially considering that the initial wait time was so short. Unfortunately, we visited on the second to last day of our trip, so we didn't have the chance to go back.

The long & short: I enjoyed Micklethwait, the ribs were good, but the brisket wasn't their best. 

We rolled in around 1:15pm to Micklethwait's cool new spot in (very) East Austin past Airport, I'm sure a cool backyard hangout on a nice day! Unfortunately it was cold and raining when we came in. Luckily though the interior was nice as well. There aren't a ton of tables, but enough that we sat down right after ordering.

The service was fine, not overly friendly, but got the job done. And they were quick with service.

Getting to the most important thing: the food. We ordered brisket (moist), spare ribs and pulled lamb. I was wavering between 3-4 on this review because the brisket wasn't the best. It was very tight & I couldn't cut through it with a fork on the thicker slice. The fat also wasn't quite a rendered as I like it. But I've had good brisket at Micklethwait's former location, so I'm going to check this up to bad luck. The crust was also solid, lots of peppery goodness.

Maybe more importantly, the ribs were really good. Nice & tender, but still a little al dente. Good smokey character as well, really great bites with either the classic or spicy sauces. And speaking of the sauces, both were top notch. I particularly liked the classic, its vinegar character provided a needed contrast to the rich & fatty meats.

Lamb seems to be popping up on more and more BBQ menus nowadays, and I'm glad it is! Micklethwait's pulled lamb was just a tad dry, but the flavor was a nice change from the typical beef/pork that characterizes Texas BBQ.

Overall recommend, but I hope they have more "good" brisket days.

photos.caption: BBQ plate: brisket (moist), pulled lamb, spare ribs, pickles/onion, sliced bread.
The backyard. Cool hangout when it's warmer than 40 and not raining

comment.text: So glad our Austin friends recommended this place. Everything was really good, but the beef rib was the best thing I've ever had. If I were to go back, I would order the beef rib and a couple sides. I particularly liked the grits, mac n cheese, and potato salad. The pickles are really good too.
Best bbq in Austin imo! The cookies are also next level and best I've ever had! I love this place so much! The hospitality is incredible too!
